title: Smart Thermostats for Older Adults: Set the Heat Once, Then Relax
subtitle: How a smart thermostat keeps the house comfortable on a schedule, what the wiring check is about, and how three current models compare.
excerpt: A smart thermostat can follow a heating schedule you set once. Here is what to check about wiring, fees and setup before you buy one, based on the makers' own pages.
author: Nickel And Gadget Editors

sections.content: Many of us know the routine. You wake up to a chilly house, shuffle to the hallway, squint at a small dial and nudge it up. At night you try to remember to turn it back down. When you leave for a few days, you wonder whether you left the heat running for no one.

A smart thermostat takes over that routine. You set a schedule once, and it warms or cools the house at the times you choose. For an older adult, or for adult children helping a parent with the house, that can mean fewer trips to the wall. It is only a thermostat, though. It does not keep an eye on a person.
A note on sources: the details below come from the makers' own product pages, which are sales pages. We have not drawn on independent reviews or testing, so treat the claims as the makers' claims.

A smart thermostat replaces the one on your wall. It connects to your home Wi-Fi, so you can use a phone app as well as the thermostat itself. You set a daily schedule, such as warmer in the morning and cooler overnight, and it follows that schedule on its own.

Google says its Nest Thermostat can turn itself down when you leave, and it also sends reminders to replace the air filter. ecobee says its Essential model avoids heating and cooling when you are away.

Wiring is the main hurdle. Both makers mention a C wire, short for common wire, which is a wire that can supply steady power to the thermostat. Older homes often lack one, and the fix can mean an add-on part. That does not rule you out, and a family member or installer can help you sort it out.

Google says the Nest Thermostat works with 85% of systems, but heating-only, cooling-only, zone-controlled and heat-pump systems require a Nest Power Connector or C wire. Google's site links to a compatibility check. For homes without a C wire, ecobee sells a Power Extender Kit for $24.99 for the Essential. ecobee says the Enhanced is compatible with most HVAC systems. If your furnace or heat pump is unusual, or you rent and cannot change wiring, a smart thermostat may not be a good fit.

A smart thermostat does not monitor anyone's health or safety. It is not a medical alert system and not a carbon monoxide alarm, and it is not a safe way to handle a heating emergency. Savings figures come from the makers, and they depend on a sensible schedule. A thermostat does not replace insulation or regular furnace maintenance.

items: Run the compatibility check first. Find out whether you have a C wire and whether you need an extra part before you buy.
Ask about fees. The product pages we used show no monthly fee, but we did not verify subscription terms, and some features may need an account or a paid plan. Read the terms on the maker's site.
Look at the screen. If you plan to use the thermostat on the wall rather than in an app, a clear touchscreen helps. ecobee describes the Essential's as an easy-to-use full-color touchscreen.
Think about hands-free control. ecobee says the Enhanced works with Amazon Alexa or Apple HomeKit.
Check the return window. ecobee says the Essential can be returned within 30 days for a full refund, and Google lists free returns for the Nest.
Plan for setup help. Wiring work is best left to a family member or professional installer. Google's Nest page offers optional pro installation.
Ask your utility about rebates. ecobee notes that eligible utility rebates are available for the Essential, which is ENERGY STAR certified.

sections.content: Setting it up and using it well
Setup often happens in an app on a phone, so it helps to have a family member nearby. Google says the Nest Thermostat has a step-by-step guide in the Google Home app. Here is how Google describes it:
"Designed for an easy setup, the step-by-step guide in the Google Home app helps you out." (Google Store, Nest Thermostat product page)
ecobee says the Enhanced takes about 45 minutes to install and includes everything needed in the box, including mounting hardware. Even so, have someone handle the wiring for you.

Once it is running, keep the schedule simple: one setting for waking, one for daytime and one for sleeping. If a parent will not use the app, a family member can set things up and show just one or two steps, such as raising the temperature a little. Write those steps on a card and keep it nearby.

Some features require a Google or ecobee account, and some advanced features may need a paid subscription. We did not verify subscription terms, so read them on the maker's site before you buy. Check current prices too, since the Nest sale price was listed as ending 11/08.
sections.label: Before You Buy

sections.content: If a simple dial suits you fine, a basic manual thermostat costs less. But if you would like the house warm when you wake and cool when you are away, without remembering to change it each day, a smart thermostat set up once can handle that routine for you.

products.name: Nest Thermostat
products.price: $89.99, marked down from $129.99; Google's page says the sale ends 11/08 (Google Store, November 2026). Check current price.
products.blurb: Schedules are set in the Google Home app with Quick Schedule, and it sends air filter reminders. Some systems, including heat pumps, require a C wire or a Nest Power Connector.

products.name: ecobee Smart Thermostat Essential
products.blurb: Has a full-color touchscreen, with schedules you can change on the thermostat or in the app. ENERGY STAR certified, with a $24.99 kit for homes without a C wire.

products.name: ecobee Smart Thermostat Enhanced
products.blurb: Works hands-free with Amazon Alexa or Apple HomeKit. It has a larger touchscreen and radar-based occupancy sensing.
